text: How could a handful of pirates capture giant merchant ships? The secret was the ship itself.
Pirates loved sloops: one mast, one giant sail, and a shallow hull that slipped into hidden coves.
Scraped clean of weeds and barnacles, a sloop could outrun almost any warship. Speed decided who lived.
Up close, they were deadly. Cannons smashed rigging, while swivel guns, muskets and cutlasses cleared the decks.
But their best weapon was fear. A black flag offered mercy. A red flag meant no quarter.
They closed fast, hooked on with grapples, and swarmed aboard before the crew could react.
In 1717, Blackbeard captured the French slave ship La Concorde and made her his flagship: Queen Anne's Revenge, armed with about forty guns.
He tucked smoking fuses under his hat, and many crews surrendered without a fight.
Fear, speed and firepower: that's what made pirate ships so dangerous.
